summary: Request: live adaptive audit feed with row-level redaction, rotating pseudonyms, and non-repudiation receipts
description: Customer requests a near-real-time audit delivery option that combines adaptive sampling with deterministic row-level redaction, rotating pseudonymization for subject identifiers, and per-event non-repudiation receipts. The feed must be consumable by their SIEM via mTLS webhook and support an S3 backup for replay. They also require hourly checkpoints containing an HMAC chain to prove ordering and completeness.
impact: CedarCloud runs security monitoring and compliance rules in their SIEM against Redwood audit events. Without a trustworthy live feed with non-repudiation and deterministic redaction, their SOC cannot meet internal evidence retention policies for regulated datasets. This is blocking go-live of their Redwood integration for production workloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enabled 'audit-stream' in Console for tenant cedarcloud-prod with default settings
2) Configured destination to customer webhook (mTLS) and S3 fallback, provided client cert
3) Observed duplicate ordering, missing 'user_id' (redacted) in 2/10 events, and no HMAC checkpoint header
4) Customer attempted to replay S3 backup but found inconsistent sequence numbers between webhook receipts and S3 manifests
sample_logs: 2026-03-09T18:03:12Z INFO audit-service: delivered event seq=12584 tenant=cedarcloud type=call.start size=764 redaction=user_id=REDACTED
2026-03-09T18:03:12Z WARN siem-connector: webhook response 202 accepted but missing-ack header for seq=12584
2026-03-09T18:04:01Z ERROR s3-uploader: manifest-mismatch expected-last=12583 actual-last=12581 tenant=cedarcloud
investigation_notes: Initial review: webhook endpoint accepted connections; mTLS client cert verified by Redwood. No immediate TLS failures in logs.
Hypothesis A: adaptive sampling engine drops metadata keys when sampling rate toggles rapidly, causing intermittent missing user_id fields.
Hypothesis B: checkpoint HMAC generation runs on a different worker than delivery; under burst, checkpoint latency leads to misaligned sequence windows.
Observed that redaction runs as a post-processing step after sampling; if sampling prunes context before redaction, pseudonymizer receives incomplete attributes.

Found an open config flag: 'emit_hmac_checkpoint=true' was set, but the HMAC key rotation window on the tenant was set to 20s which caused worker A to sign with key v3 while worker B rotated to v4 mid-window. This explains checkpoint verification failures in customer's verifier.
Customer's SIEM expects a header 'X-RW-Ack: seq' to confirm receipt; our connector sets 'X-RW-Receipt' instead — mismatch in naming is causing their ingest playbook to mark messages unacknowledged.
customer_comments: (CedarCloud SOC) 2026-03-10T09:17Z: We need per-event deterministic pseudonyms so our correlation rules can join sessions across multiple feeds. Random salts break our joins.
(CedarCloud Eng) 2026-03-11T14:02Z: The S3 backup manifest must include contiguous sequence ranges and epoch timestamps; we currently see overlaps when delivery retries occur.

(CedarCloud Compliance) 2026-03-11T18:45Z: For audits we need a signed proof of ordering that we can store offsite for 3 years. Can Redwood provide an attested hourly checkpoint file signed with a customer-trusted key?
support_comments: (Support) 2026-03-11T10:05Z: Reproduced missing user_id locally by toggling adaptive sampling from 1.0 -> 0.1 -> 1.0 in <5s. Filed INT-229 to track worker-local cache race.
(SRE) 2026-03-12T07:30Z: Identified key rotation race; will add a coordinator to guarantee checkpoint signing uses stable key for the checkpoint window.

(Platform Eng) 2026-03-12T15:21Z: Agreed to add an optional 'X-RW-Ack' header alias for webhook delivery for compatibility with legacy SIEM playbooks; SDK patch linked in PR. See github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/418
proposed_workaround: Enable tenant-level 'deterministic-pseudonyms' (preview) and set adaptive-sampling.min_interval=30s to reduce sampling toggles. Temporarily configure SIEM to accept 'X-RW-Receipt' as an alias for 'X-RW-Ack'.
resolution: Work items completed: (1) Added coordinator to checkpoint signer to avoid key-rotation races; checkpoints now signed with stable key per-hour. (2) Implemented 'X-RW-Ack' alias and documented header mapping in Confluence. (3) Introduced an option 'deterministic-pseudonym: true' that uses tenant-stable salt with rotation policy; SDK updated and deployed to prod-us-east. Customer validated end-to-end on 2026-03-12 and confirmed SIEM accepted events and hourly checkpoints verified.
follow_up_actions: 1) Product: GA feature for deterministic pseudonyms and public doc for rotation policy (owner: ProductManager - due 2026-04-01)
2) Docs: Update SIEM onboarding checklist to include header alias and recommended sampling settings (owner: DX - due 2026-03-20)
3) SRE: Add automated e2e test that simulates rapid sampling toggles and verifies S3 manifest sequence consistency (owner: SRE Lead - due 2026-03-25)
4) Security: Provide a short attestation template that CedarCloud can store with hourly checkpoint signatures (owner: Security Eng - due 2026-03-18)
public_note: Delivered interim workaround and roadmap for full fix. Customer is in agreement and has scheduled a follow-up validation session on 2026-03-16.
